He showed me men sitting on a bench and another man sitting on a chair. He asked, “Do you see the men on the bench?” “I see them, sir,” I said. “They are faithful,” he said. “The man on the chair is a false prophet. He destroys the understanding of God’s servants who waver, but not of those who are faithful.”[a]

2. People who waver go to him as they would to a magician. They ask what will happen to them. The false prophet has no power of a divine spirit in himself. He speaks according to their questions and their wicked desires. He fills their souls as they wish.[c]

3. He is empty, so he gives empty answers to empty people. Whatever they ask, he answers according to their emptiness. He does say some true words. The devil fills him with his own spirit, hoping to tear some of the righteous away.

4. Those who are strong in the Lord’s faith have put on the truth. They keep away from such spirits. But people who waver and often change their minds[b] practice divination like the nations. They commit idolatry and bring greater sin upon themselves. Anyone who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of truth and foolish.

5. No spirit given by God is consulted. It has the power of divinity and speaks everything from itself. It comes from above, from the divine spirit’s power.[d]

6. A spirit that answers questions according to people’s desires is earthly and light. It has no power. It does not speak at all unless someone consults it.

7. “Sir, how can a person tell a prophet from a false prophet?” I asked. He said, “Listen about both. What I am about to say will show you how to test them. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.”

8. “First, the man with the [divine] spirit from above is gentle, quiet and humble. He keeps away from every evil and this age’s empty desires. He makes himself lower than everyone. He gives no answer when consulted and does not speak privately. The holy Spirit does not speak whenever a person wants to speak. It speaks when God wants the man to speak.”

9. “The man with the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit. They offer intercession to God. Then the angel of the prophetic spirit assigned to him fills the man. Filled with the holy Spirit, he speaks to the gathering as the Lord wishes.”[e]

10. “This is how the spirit of divinity becomes clear. Such is the power of the Lord’s spirit of divinity.”

11. “Now listen about the earthly, empty spirit. It has no power and is foolish.”

12. “The man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself. He wants the first seat. He is immediately presumptuous, shameless and talkative. He lives in many luxuries and other deceits. He takes payment for his prophecy. If he is not paid, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit take payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this. Such prophets have an earthly spirit.”

13. “He does not go near a gathering of righteous men at all. Instead, he avoids them. He stays close to people who waver and are empty. He prophesies to them in a corner. He deceives them with empty words that suit their desires. He gives empty people answers. An empty vessel placed with other empty vessels does not break. They agree with one another.”

14. “But he may enter a gathering full of righteous men who have the spirit of divinity. When they offer intercession, that man is emptied. The earthly spirit flees from him in fear. The man becomes speechless. He is completely shattered and cannot say anything.”[f]

15. “Suppose you pack a storeroom with wine or oil and put an empty jar among them. Later, when you unpack the room, you find that jar still empty. It is the same with empty prophets. When they come among the spirits of the righteous, they are found just as they came.”

16. “You have the way of life of both kinds of prophets. Test the man who says he bears a spirit by his life and works.”[g]

17. “Trust the spirit that comes from God and has power. Do not trust the earthly, empty spirit. It has no power and comes from the devil.”

18. “Listen to this parable. Take a stone and throw it toward heaven. See whether you can touch heaven. Or take a water tube and squirt water toward heaven. See whether you can pierce heaven.”[h]

19. “How can these things happen, sir?” I asked. “You have said both are impossible.” He said, “Just as these are impossible, earthly spirits are powerless and inactive.”

20. “Now consider the power that comes from above. A hailstone is a very small pellet. Yet how much pain it causes when it falls on a person’s head! Or consider a drop that falls from a roof tile to the ground. It bores through stone.”

21. “Very small things falling from above onto the earth have great power. In the same way, the divine spirit coming from above is powerful. Trust this spirit and keep away from the other.”

    αὐτὸν τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς· κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου,

    δύναμιν· τῷ δὲ πνεύματι τῷ ἐπιγείῳ καὶ κενῷ μηδὲν πίστευε, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν· ἀπὸ τοῦ
    διαβόλου γὰρ ἔρχεται. 18. ἄκουσον [οὖν] τὴν παραβολὴν ἣν μέλλω σοι λέγειν. λάβε λίθον καὶ βάλε εἰς
    τὸν οὐρανόν, ἴδε εἰ δύνασαι ἅψασθαι αὐτοῦ· ἢ πάλιν λάβε σίφωνα ὕδατος καὶ σιφώνισον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν,
    ἴδε εἰ δύνασαι τρυπῆσαι τὸν οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα
    ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ
    ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν
    ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαί,
    καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον. 21. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει·

    ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.

  text: '1. He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. And he says to me,
    “Do you see the ones sitting on the bench?” “I see, sir,” I say. “These,” he says, “are faithful;
    and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants
    of God—of the double‑minded, not of the faithful.[a]


    2. These, then, the double‑minded, come to him as to a magician and ask him what will happen to them;
    and that false prophet, having in himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according
    to their questions [and according to the desires of their wickedness], and fills their souls as they
    desire.[c]


    3. For he, being empty, answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers
    according to the emptiness of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills
    him with his own spirit, if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.


    4. Therefore, as many as are strong in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling
    to such spirits, but keep away from them. But those who are double‑minded and often change their minds[b]
    practice divination like the nations and bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry;
    for the one who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.


    5. For no spirit given from God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything
    from itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.[d]


    6. But the spirit that is consulted and speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light,
    having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is consulted.


    7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?”

    \ and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants\

    \ himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according to their questions [and according\
    \ to the desires of their wickedness], and fills their souls as they desire.\n\n3. For he, being empty,\
    \ answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers according to the emptiness\
    \ of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills him with his own spirit,\
    \ if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.\n\n4. Therefore, as many as are strong\
    \ in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits, but keep away from\
    \ them. But those who are double‑minded and often repent practice divination like the nations and\
    \ bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry; for the one who consults a false prophet\
    \ about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.\n\n5. For no spirit given from\
    \ God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything from itself, because\
    \ it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.\n\n6. But the spirit that is consulted and\
    \ speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light, having no power; and it does not speak\
    \ at all unless it is consulted.\n\n7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is\
    \ a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Listen,” he says, “about both prophets; and in the way\
    \ I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has\
    \ the divine spirit by his life.\n\n8. First of all, the one who has the [divine] spirit from above\
    \ is gentle and quiet and humble‑minded, and refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of\
    \ this age, and makes himself lower than all people; and when consulted he answers nothing to anyone,\
    \ nor does he speak privately—nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes it to speak—but\
    \ it speaks when God wishes him to speak.\n\n9. Therefore, when the man who has the divine spirit\
    \ comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and an intercession\
    \ is made to God by the gathering of those men, then the angel of the prophetic spirit who is assigned\

    \ wills.\n\n10. Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest. As for the spirit of the Deity\
    \ of the Lord, this is its power.\n\n11. “Hear now,” he says, “about the spirit that is earthly and\
    \ empty and has no power, but is foolish.\n\n12. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts\
    \ himself and wants to have the first seat; and immediately he is presumptuous and shameless and talkative,\
    \ and lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he receives payment for his prophecy;\
    \ and if he does not receive it, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit receive payment and prophesy?\
    \ A prophet of God cannot do this; rather, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.\n\n13. Then, he\
    \ does not come near a gathering of righteous men at all, but avoids them. He clings to the double‑minded\
    \ and the empty, and he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking everything according\
    \ to their desires, emptily; for he also answers the empty. For an empty vessel, placed together with\
    \ empty ones, is not broken, but they agree with one another.\n\n14. [Heaven.] \n\n19. “How,” I say,\
    \ “sir, can these things be? For you have said both these things are impossible.” “As these, then,\
    \ are impossible, so also the spirits that are earthly are impossible and inert.\n\n20. Take now the\
    \ power that comes from above. Hail is a very small pellet, and when it falls on a man’s head, how\

    \ upon the earth, have great power; so also the divine spirit that comes from above is powerful. Trust\
    \ in this spirit[a][21][14][10][9][8], but keep away from the other.”"

  text: Ἔδειξέ μοι ἐπὶ συμψελλίου καθημένους ἀνθρώπους, καὶ ἕτερον ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ καθέδραν. καὶ
    λέγει μοι· Βλέπεις τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελλίου καθημένους; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε. Οὗτοι, φησί, πιστοί εἰσι,
    καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν καθέδραν ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστὶν [ὃς] ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ Θεοῦ·
    τῶν διψύχων δὲ ἀπόλλυσιν, οὐ τῶν πιστῶν. 2. οὗτοι οὖν οἱ δίψυχοι ὡς ἐπὶ μάγον ἔρχονται, καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν
    αὐτὸν τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς· κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου,
    λαλεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὰ ἐπερωτήματα αὐτῶν | [καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς πονηρίας αὐτῶν], καὶ πληροῖ
    τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν |, καθὼς αὐτοὶ βούλονται. 3. αὐτὸς γὰρ κενὸς ὢν κενὰ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται κενοῖς· ὃ γὰρ
    ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇ, πρὸς τὸ κένωμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκρίνεται. τινὰ δὲ καὶ ῥήματα ἀληθῆ λαλεῖ· ὁ γὰρ διάβολος
    πληροῖ αὐτὸν τῷ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι, εἴ τινα δυνήσεται ῥῆξαι τῶν δικαίων. 4. ὅσοι οὖν ἰσχυροί εἰσιν ἐν
    τῇ πίστει τοῦ Κυρίου ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται
    ἀπ’ αὐτῶν. ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἑαυτοῖς μείζονα
    ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιφέρουσιν εἰδωλολατροῦντες· ὁ γὰρ ἐπερωτῶν ψευδοπροφήτην περὶ πράξεώς τινος εἰδωλολάτρης
    ἐστὶ καὶ κενὸς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἄφρων. 5. πᾶν γὰρ πνεῦμα ἀπὸ Θεοῦ δοθὲν οὐκ ἐπερωτᾶται, ἀλλὰ ἔχον
    τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ πάντα, ὅτι ἄνωθέν ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θείου πνεύματος.
    6. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπερωτώμενον καὶ λαλοῦν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπίγειόν ἐστι καὶ ἐλαφρόν,
    δύναμιν μὴ ἔχον· καὶ ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ ἐὰν μὴ ἐπερωτηθῇ. 7. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται τίς
    αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν· καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω
    λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν
    ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον. 8. πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος

    προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα. 13. εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει

    κενόν, καὶ πάλιν ἀποστιβάσαι θελήσῃς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ κεράμιον ἐκεῖνο, ὃ ἔθηκας κενόν, κενὸν καὶ εὑρήσεις·

    16. ἔχεις ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν τὴν ζωήν. δοκίμαζε οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς καὶ τῶν ἔργων τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν

    δύναμιν· τῷ δὲ πνεύματι τῷ ἐπιγείῳ καὶ κενῷ μηδὲν πίστευε, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν· ἀπὸ τοῦ

    ἴδε εἰ δύνασαι τρυπῆσαι τὸν οὐρανόν. 19. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα

    ἀδρανῆ. 20. λάβε νῦν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην. ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν

translation:
  text: 'He showed me men sitting on a bench and another man sitting on a chair. He asked, “Do you see
    the men on the bench?” “I see them, sir,” I said. “They are faithful,” he said. “The man on the chair
    is a false prophet. He destroys the understanding of God’s servants who waver, but not of those who
    are faithful.”[a]


    2. People who waver go to him as they would to a magician. They ask what will happen to them. The
    false prophet has no power of a divine spirit in himself. He speaks according to their questions and
    their wicked desires. He fills their souls as they wish.[c]


    3. He is empty, so he gives empty answers to empty people. Whatever they ask, he answers according
    to their emptiness. He does say some true words. The devil fills him with his own spirit, hoping to
    tear some of the righteous away.


    4. Those who are strong in the Lord’s faith have put on the truth. They keep away from such spirits.
    But people who waver and often change their minds[b] practice divination like the nations. They commit
    idolatry and bring greater sin upon themselves. Anyone who consults a false prophet about any matter
    is an idolater, empty of truth and foolish.


    5. No spirit given by God is consulted. It has the power of divinity and speaks everything from itself.
    It comes from above, from the divine spirit’s power.[d]


    6. A spirit that answers questions according to people’s desires is earthly and light. It has no power.
    It does not speak at all unless someone consults it.


    7. “Sir, how can a person tell a prophet from a false prophet?” I asked. He said, “Listen about both.
    What I am about to say will show you how to test them. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his
    life.”


    8. “First, the man with the [divine] spirit from above is gentle, quiet and humble. He keeps away
    from every evil and this age’s empty desires. He makes himself lower than everyone. He gives no answer
    when consulted and does not speak privately. The holy Spirit does not speak whenever a person wants
    to speak. It speaks when God wants the man to speak.”


    9. “The man with the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine
    Spirit. They offer intercession to God. Then the angel of the prophetic spirit assigned to him fills
    the man. Filled with the holy Spirit, he speaks to the gathering as the Lord wishes.”[e]


    10. “This is how the spirit of divinity becomes clear. Such is the power of the Lord’s spirit of divinity.”


    11. “Now listen about the earthly, empty spirit. It has no power and is foolish.”


    12. “The man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself. He wants the first seat. He is immediately
    presumptuous, shameless and talkative. He lives in many luxuries and other deceits. He takes payment
    for his prophecy. If he is not paid, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit take payment and prophesy?
    A prophet of God cannot do this. Such prophets have an earthly spirit.”


    13. “He does not go near a gathering of righteous men at all. Instead, he avoids them. He stays close
    to people who waver and are empty. He prophesies to them in a corner. He deceives them with empty
    words that suit their desires. He gives empty people answers. An empty vessel placed with other empty
    vessels does not break. They agree with one another.”


    14. “But he may enter a gathering full of righteous men who have the spirit of divinity. When they
    offer intercession, that man is emptied. The earthly spirit flees from him in fear. The man becomes
    speechless. He is completely shattered and cannot say anything.”[f]


    15. “Suppose you pack a storeroom with wine or oil and put an empty jar among them. Later, when you
    unpack the room, you find that jar still empty. It is the same with empty prophets. When they come
    among the spirits of the righteous, they are found just as they came.”


    16. “You have the way of life of both kinds of prophets. Test the man who says he bears a spirit by
    his life and works.”[g]


    17. “Trust the spirit that comes from God and has power. Do not trust the earthly, empty spirit. It
    has no power and comes from the devil.”


    18. “Listen to this parable. Take a stone and throw it toward heaven. See whether you can touch heaven.
    Or take a water tube and squirt water toward heaven. See whether you can pierce heaven.”[h]


    19. “How can these things happen, sir?” I asked. “You have said both are impossible.” He said, “Just
    as these are impossible, earthly spirits are powerless and inactive.”


    20. “Now consider the power that comes from above. A hailstone is a very small pellet. Yet how much
    pain it causes when it falls on a person’s head! Or consider a drop that falls from a roof tile to
    the ground. It bores through stone.”


    21. “Very small things falling from above onto the earth have great power. In the same way, the divine
    spirit coming from above is powerful. Trust this spirit and keep away from the other.”'

  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working 1891 text has dianoian, “understanding.” Lake (1907), Plate VIII, prints dynamin,
      “power,” in its Athos transcription. Alternative: “The false prophet destroys the power of God’s
      servants who waver, not of those who are faithful.” This printed transcription difference is recorded
      pending fresh manuscript photograph verification; it is not silently substituted into the working
      Greek.'
  - marker: b
    text: 'Reconsideration of the prior lexical decision: “change their minds” is kept provisionally because
      the passage links frequent changes of mind with wavering and divination. “Often repent” is another
      possible translation. The passage does not say which way they change or mention baptism. Repentance
      means more than feeling sorry; a turn toward God is not added here.'
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working edition bars the span from the added wicked-desires clause through “fills their
      souls,” and brackets the wicked-desires clause within it. Athos, Lake (1907), Plate VIII, has the
      longer wording. Shorter alternative: “He speaks with them according to their questions, as they
      wish.” The draft retains the longer working wording with its uncertainty exposed; the bar and bracket
      layers remain distinct in the source. The older 1891 apparatus reports an Athos omission here, while
      Lake’s later transcription prints the longer span. This disagreement between reports requires a
      fresh photo check; it does not certify every supplied letter.'
  - marker: d
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: '“Is consulted” renders the question-and-answer setting, not a prohibition on all prayer. Alternative:
      “For every spirit given by God is not consulted.” The source contrasts divine initiative with speech
      supplied on demand. The chapter’s divinity language does not itself require replacing each spirit
      with a later doctrinal formula.'
  - marker: e
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Angel of the prophetic spirit” is Hilgenfeld’s printed conjecture, not Athos’s wording. Athos,
      Lake Plate VIII, has “angel of the prophet.” Full alternative: “Then the angel of the prophet, assigned
      to him, fills the man; filled with the holy Spirit, the man speaks to the multitude as the Lord
      wills.” The draft provisionally retains the working phrase and records the shorter Greek alternative.
      Earlier in this paragraph, “faith in the divine Spirit” can also be translated “faith from the divine
      Spirit” or “spirit-given faith.” These alternatives understand the Spirit as the source of the faith
      rather than its object.'
  - marker: f
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'Earthly is the working edition’s correction supported by both Latin traditions: Vulgata spiritus
      ille terrestris, Hilgenfeld (1873), physical p. 79 printed p. 62, and Palatina spiritus terrenus,
      Gebhardt/Harnack (1877), physical p. 218 printed p. 121. Athos, Lake Plate VIII, instead reads holy:
      “The holy spirit flees from him out of fear.” The correction fits the repeated contrast in paragraphs
      6, 11–12, 17 and 19; it is not preserved Athos Greek. Other working corrections in this sentence
      include spirit-of-divinity and intercession by them against Athos most-divine-spirit and by it (the
      gathering). Athos also has a different incapacitation verb; becoming speechless is the version-supported
      working reading. These editions mediate manuscript evidence, not new manuscript photographs or independent
      votes per edition.'
  - marker: g
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working order “life and works” is editorial; Athos has “works and life.” Alternative: “Test
      by his works and life the man who says he bears a spirit.” Pneumatophoros means spirit-bearing.
      The Latin editions expand the claimed spirit as holy; the working Greek does not have that adjective
      here, so it is not added to the English.'
  - marker: h
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: Siphōn denotes the water tube or squirting apparatus in the illustration. The draft does not
      specify a modern mechanism or weapon. Heaven can also be rendered sky; the image concerns reaching
      and piercing it from below. The following “both are impossible” now has its two missing examples
      restored. The working “then” at this paragraph’s opening is bracketed and absent from Athos.
lexical_decisions:
- source_word: συμψελλίον
  chosen: bench
  alternatives:
  - bench‑seat
  - settle
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: A low shared seat; “bench” captures a communal sitting surface distinguished from a single
    chair (καθέδρα).
- source_word: καθέδρα
  chosen: chair
  alternatives:
  - seat
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Concrete furniture term; “chair” contrasts with the bench and underscores the false prophet’s
    singled‑out position.
- source_word: ψευδοπροφήτης
  chosen: false prophet
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Standard, transparent rendering for a claimant to prophecy who is false.
- source_word: διάνοια
  chosen: understanding
  alternatives:
  - mind
  - discernment
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: In context, what is being ruined is the capacity to judge rightly; “understanding” fits well.
- source_word: δοῦλοι (τοῦ Θεοῦ)
  chosen: God’s servants
  alternatives:
  - servants of God
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Reconsideration of the prior lexical decision: current servant policy uses “God’s servants”
    here. The Greek δοῦλοι retains bonded-status, belonging and allegiance to God as explanatory nuance;
    that nuance does not require changing the reader wording to “slaves.”'
- source_word: δίψυχος
  chosen: double‑minded
  alternatives:
  - two‑souled
  - vacillating
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Established moral term in Hermas; “double‑minded” preserves idiom and his recurring vice
    list.
- source_word: μάγος
  chosen: magician
  alternatives:
  - sorcerer
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Hermas contrasts prophecy with divinatory magic; “magician” is the clearest modern equivalent.
- source_word: ἐπερωτάω
  chosen: consult
  alternatives:
  - question
  - inquire of
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: In context of seeking future knowledge from a seer; “consult” communicates the divinatory
    act.
- source_word: πνεῦμα θεῖον / τὸ τῆς θεότητος
  chosen: divine spirit / the spirit of the Deity
  alternatives:
  - God’s Spirit
  - divine Spirit
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Hermas distinguishes adjectives (theios vs. hagios). Rendering preserves the nuance of divinity/Deity.
- source_word: πνεῦμα ἅγιον
  chosen: holy Spirit
  alternatives:
  - Holy Spirit
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Retains adjective “holy” explicitly; capitalization lightly varied to reflect Greek adjective,
    not a proper name.
- source_word: κενός
  chosen: empty
  alternatives:
  - vain
  - hollow
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Key motif (emptiness) contrasted with fullness of the divine spirit; keep consistent literal
    term.
- source_word: ῥῆξαι (from ῥήγνυμι)
  chosen: tear away
  alternatives:
  - rend
  - snatch away
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Violent metaphor for pulling some of the righteous away; “tear away” is vivid yet accurate.
- source_word: ἐνδύω (ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν)
  chosen: having put on the truth
  alternatives:
  - clothed with the truth
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Clothing metaphor is important in Hermas; “put on” preserves the verb.
- source_word: μετανοέω
  chosen: change their minds
  alternatives:
  - repent
  - change their mind
  lexicon: Recorded source/witness and contextual review; see docs/REPENTANCE_REASSESSMENT_2026-10-13.md
  rationale: 'Reconsideration of the prior lexical decision: retain “change their minds” provisionally
    because frequent μετανοοῦσι is associated here with double-mindedness and divination. “Repent” remains
    a lexical alternative. The clause neither identifies baptism nor explicitly states the direction of
    the change; the vacillation reading is contextual interpretation, not independent scholarly certification.'
  doctrine_reference: 'DOCTRINE.md: Repentance terminology (2026-10-13)'
- source_word: μαντεύομαι
  chosen: practice divination
  alternatives:
  - consult oracles
  - divine
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Pagan divinatory practice; “practice divination” is precise.
- source_word: εἰδωλολατρεῖν
  chosen: worship idols
  alternatives:
  - be idolaters
  - practice idolatry
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Verbal form; “worship idols” keeps active sense that incurs guilt.
- source_word: θεότης
  chosen: Deity
  alternatives:
  - divine nature
  - Godhead
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: “Deity” is transparent and contemporary while retaining metaphysical weight; avoids archaic
    “Godhead.”
- source_word: ἔντευξις
  chosen: petition
  alternatives:
  - entreaty
  - prayer
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Formal communal prayer; “petition” fits the setting of a gathering appealing to God.
- source_word: ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος
  chosen: angel of the prophetic spirit
  alternatives:
  - angel assigned to the prophetic spirit
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Literal rendering preserves Hermas’s angelology linking prophetic inspiration with angelic
    oversight.
- source_word: ὑψοῦν ἑαυτόν
  chosen: exalts himself
  alternatives:
  - puffs himself up
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Moral self‑promotion opposed to humility; “exalts himself” echoes biblical idiom without
    importing NT phrasing unduly.
- source_word: ἰταμός
  chosen: presumptuous
  alternatives:
  - impetuous
  - insolent
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Conveys forward, rash boldness fitting the false prophet’s demeanor.
- source_word: ἀναιδής
  chosen: shameless
  alternatives:
  - impudent
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Moral lack of shame is in view; “shameless” is clear.
- source_word: πολύλαλος
  chosen: talkative
  alternatives:
  - a babbler
  - wordy
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Describes verbosity; “talkative” is simple and accurate.
- source_word: τρυφή
  chosen: luxury
  alternatives:
  - self‑indulgence
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Lifestyle of ease and indulgence; “luxury” fits plural “many luxuries.”
- source_word: ἀπάτη
  chosen: deceit
  alternatives:
  - trickery
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: General term for deceptive practices.
- source_word: μισθός
  chosen: payment
  alternatives:
  - wages
  - fee
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Remuneration received for prophecy; “payment” covers the sense without implying employment
    (wages).
- source_word: συναγωγή
  chosen: gathering
  alternatives:
  - assembly
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: General assembly; avoids anachronistic association with the Jewish synagogue while keeping
    literal sense.
- source_word: κατὰ γωνίαν
  chosen: in a corner
  alternatives:
  - privately
  - in secret
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Concrete image of skulking prophecy away from the gathered righteous; literal but intelligible.
- source_word: συμφωνεῖν
  chosen: agree
  alternatives:
  - harmonize
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: “Agree with one another” fits the vessel metaphor plainly.
- source_word: ἀδρανής
  chosen: inert
  alternatives:
  - inactive
  - powerless
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Captures lack of effective power; pairs well with “earthly” and “light.”
- source_word: χάλαζα
  chosen: hail
  alternatives:
  - hailstone
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Collective used as countable in context; “hail” as a small pellet is familiar.
- source_word: κεράμος
  chosen: roof tile
  alternatives:
  - tile
  lexicon: LSJ

base_translation:
  text: '1. He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. And he says to me,
    “Do you see the ones sitting on the bench?” “I see, sir,” I say. “These,” he says, “are faithful;
    and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants
    of God—of the double‑minded, not of the faithful.[a]


    2. These, then, the double‑minded, come to him as to a magician and ask him what will happen to them;
    and that false prophet, having in himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according
    to their questions [and according to the desires of their wickedness], and fills their souls as they
    desire.[c]


    3. For he, being empty, answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers
    according to the emptiness of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills
    him with his own spirit, if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.


    4. Therefore, as many as are strong in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling
    to such spirits, but keep away from them. But those who are double‑minded and often change their minds[b]
    practice divination like the nations and bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry;
    for the one who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.


    5. For no spirit given from God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything
    from itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.[d]


    6. But the spirit that is consulted and speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light,
    having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is consulted.


    7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?”
    “Listen,” he says, “about both prophets; and in the way I am about to tell you, so you shall test
    the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.


    8. First of all, the one who has the [divine] spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble‑minded,
    and refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of this age, and makes himself lower than all
    people; and when consulted he answers nothing to anyone, nor does he speak privately—nor does the
    holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes to speak—but it speaks when God wishes him to speak.


    9. Therefore, when the man who has the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have
    faith in the divine Spirit, and an intercession is made to God by the gathering of those men, then
    the angel of the prophetic spirit who is assigned to him fills the man; and being filled with the
    holy Spirit he speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.[e]


    10. Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest. As for the spirit of the Deity of the Lord,
    this is its power.


    11. “Hear now,” he says, “about the spirit that is earthly and empty and has no power, but is foolish.


    12. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the first seat; and
    immediately he is presumptuous and shameless and talkative, and lives among many luxuries and many
    other deceits, and he receives payment for his prophecy; and if he does not receive it, he does not
    prophesy. Can a divine spirit receive payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this; rather,
    the spirit of such prophets is earthly.


    13. Then, he does not come near a gathering of righteous men at all, but avoids them. He clings to
    the double‑minded and the empty, and he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking
    everything according to their desires, emptily; for he also answers the empty. For an empty vessel,
    placed together with empty ones, is not broken, but they agree with one another.


    14. But when he comes into a gathering full of righteous men who have the spirit of divinity, and
    they offer intercession, that man is emptied. The earthly spirit flees from him out of fear, and the
    man becomes speechless and is completely shattered, unable to say anything.[f]


    15. For if you pack a storeroom with wine or oil and place an empty jar among them, then later wish
    to unpack the storeroom, you will find the jar you placed there empty still. So too, when empty prophets
    come among the spirits of the righteous, they are found just as they came.


    16. You have the way of life of both kinds of prophets. So test by his life and works the man who
    says that he bears a spirit.[g]


    17. But you must trust the spirit that comes from God and has power. Put no trust in the earthly and
    empty spirit, because it has no power; it comes from the devil.


    18. Listen, then, to the parable I am about to tell you. Take a stone and throw it toward heaven;
    see whether you can touch heaven. Or take a water tube and squirt water toward heaven; see whether
    you can pierce heaven.[h]


    19. “How,” I say, “sir, can these things be? For you have said both these things are impossible.”
    “As these, then, are impossible, so also the spirits that are earthly are powerless and inert.


    20. Take now the power that comes from above. Hail is a very small pellet, and when it falls on a
    man’s head, how much pain it causes! Or again, take a drop that falls from the roof tile to the ground,
    and it bores through the stone.


    21. You see, then, that things from above, though very small when they fall upon the earth, have great
    power; so also the divine spirit that comes from above is powerful. Trust in this spirit, but keep
    away from the other.”'
